{{Short description|Class of inequalities}}
In [[mathematics]],  '''logarithmic Sobolev inequalities''' are a class of inequalities involving the norm of a function <math>f</math>, its logarithm, and its gradient <math>\nabla f </math>. These inequalities were discovered and named by [[Leonard Gross]], who established them in dimension-independent form,<ref>{{harvnb|Gross|1975a}}</ref><ref>{{harvnb|Gross|1975b}}</ref> in the context of [[constructive quantum field theory]]. Similar results were discovered by other mathematicians before and many variations on such inequalities are known.

Gross<ref>{{harvnb|Gross|1975a}}</ref> proved the inequality:

<math display="block">
\int_{\mathbb{R}^n}\big|f(x)\big|^2 \log\big|f(x)\big| \,d\nu(x) \leq \int_{\mathbb{R}^n}\big|\nabla f(x)\big|^2  \,d\nu(x) +\|f\|_2^2\log \|f\|_2,
</math>

where <math> \|f\|_2</math> is the <math> L^2(\nu)</math>-norm of <math>f</math>, with <math>\nu</math> being standard [[Gaussian measure]] on <math>  \mathbb{R}^n. </math>  Unlike classical [[Sobolev inequalities]], Gross's log-Sobolev inequality does not have any dimension-dependent constant, which makes it applicable in the infinite-dimensional limit.

== Entropy functional ==
Define the entropy functional<math display="block">\operatorname{Ent}_\mu(f) = \int (f \ln f) d\mu - \int f \ln \left(\int f d\mu\right) d\mu</math>This is equal to the (unnormalized) [[Kullback–Leibler divergence|KL divergence]] by <math display="inline">\operatorname{Ent}_\mu(f) = D_{KL}(f d \mu \| (\int f  d\mu) d\mu)</math>. 

A probability measure <math>\mu</math> on <math>\mathbb{R}^n</math> is said to satisfy the log-Sobolev inequality with constant <math>C>0</math> if for any smooth function ''f''
<math display="block">
\operatorname{Ent}_\mu(f^2) \le C \int_{\mathbb{R}^n} \big|\nabla f(x)\big|^2\,d\mu(x),
</math>

== Variants ==
{{Math theorem
| name = Lemma
| note = {{harv|Tao|2012|loc=Lemma 2.1.16}}
| math_statement = Let <math display="inline">X_1, \dots, X_n</math> be random variables that are independent, complex-valued, and bounded. <math display="inline">F: \mathbf{C}^n \rightarrow \mathbf{R}</math> be a smooth convex function. Then

<math display="block">
\mathbf{E} F(X) e^{F(X)} \leq\left(\mathbf{E} e^{F(X)}\right)\left(\log \mathbf{E} e^{F(X)}\right)+C \mathbf{E} e^{F(X)}|\nabla F(X)|^2
</math>

for some absolute constant <math display="inline">C</math> (independent of <math display="inline">n</math>).
}}
